summary: This article explains how drones fly without a pilot on board, the jobs they do on farms, in rescues, and in deliveries, and the rules that keep them safe.
introduce: Read the title “Drones at Work” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a part with spinning blades that pushes air or water to move a machine
a device that notices things like heat, light, or movement
to take something to a person or place

challengeTerms.def: to find the way from one place to another
a machine that circles Earth in space and sends signals

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that drones do more good than harm? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a drone flies and describe two jobs it can do.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review propeller, sensor, and deliver, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use navigate, satellite, and thermal in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
